name: Hochgurgl
kurzbeschreibung: Hochgurgl at 2,150 m altitude in the upper Ötztal: Top Mountain Crosspoint with Europe's highest motorcycle museum and toll station to Timmelsjoch.
preis: Erwachsene 15,00 €, Kinder 8,00 € (mit Ötztal Summer Card kostenlos)
oeffnungszeiten: Museum täglich 10:00–17:00 Uhr (Sommer Mai–Nov, Winter Dez–Apr)
beschreibung:
Overview

The high-alpine hotel and ski village Hochgurgl sits perched at an altitude of 2,150 meters on a sunny slope terrace in the innermost Ötztal. Together with the neighboring village of Obergurgl, the settlement forms the renowned tourism region of Gurgl – known as the "Diamond of the Alps". Framed by 21 glaciated three-thousand-meter peaks of the Ötztal and Stubai Alps, Hochgurgl is not only one of the highest winter sports destinations in the entire Alpine region, but also the spectacular gateway to the world-famous Timmelsjoch Hochalpenstraße, which connects North Tyrol with the South Tyrolean Passeiertal across the 2,509-meter-high mountain pass.

Top Mountain Crosspoint & Motorcycle Museum

The architectural and cultural center is the Top Mountain Crosspoint at 2,175 meters altitude, opened in 2016 and rebuilt following a fire in 2021. Designed by renowned architect Michael Brötz, the futuristic multifunctional building with curved wooden facades combines four functions under one roof: the valley station of the 10-seater gondola Kirchenkarbahn, the toll station for the Timmelsjoch high alpine road, a first-class panorama restaurant, and Europe's highest motorcycle museum. The Top Mountain Motorcycle Museum delights motorsport enthusiasts from across the globe across more than 4,500 m² of exhibition space. Founded by passionate collector brothers Alban und Attila Scheiber, the museum exhibits over 500 historic motorcycles and rare racing classics from more than 100 legendary marques – including gems from Brough Superior, Vincent, Ducati, Indian, BMW, and Harley-Davidson, as well as vintage sports cars. The exhibition is complemented by the Motor-Experience cinema and interactive technology stations.

Visit & Getting There

The Top Mountain Motorcycle Museum and panorama restaurant are open daily from 10:00 to 17:00 in summer (mid-May to early November) and in winter (December to April) (restaurant from 09:00; last entry to museum at 16:30). Museum admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €15.00, children €8.00; with the regional Ötztal Summer Card or a valid 6-day ski pass, museum entry is free of charge! Parking at the Crosspoint is free for visitors. Arrival by car: from the north via the Inntal motorway A12, exit Ötztal, follow the B186 approximately 50 km into the valley through Sölden to Hochgurgl; in summer the trip can be continued across the toll pass Timmelsjoch to Merano. By public transport: ÖBB train to Ötztal-Bahnhof station, then take the VVT bus route 4194 (Ötztaler Linienbus) directly to the stop Hochgurgl Top Mountain Crosspoint.

Tips

The entire building of the Top Mountain Crosspoint is exemplarily barrier-free, equipped with modern elevators and wheelchair-accessible ramps for all visitors. Take a seat on the sunny viewing terrace and enjoy a wood-fired pizza or regional game specialties while taking in the panorama of the Königskogel peaks. In summer, continuing your drive along the Timmelsjoch Hochalpenstraße with its sculptural architectural stations is highly worthwhile.
